## Proof

Let $\mathcal{M}_{n+1}[a,b]$ denote the set of **monic polynomials of degree $n+1$** on $[a,b]$, and let
$$\|Q\|_{\infty,[a,b]} := \sup_{x\in[a,b]}|Q(x)|.$$

**Key observation.** Both sides of the claimed equality are infima of $\|Q\|_{\infty,[a,b]}$ over subsets of $\mathcal{M}_{n+1}[a,b]$:

- For the **right side**: $x^{n+1}-P(x)$ with $P\in\mathcal{P}_n$ ranges over *all* monic polynomials of degree $n+1$ (every monic polynomial $Q$ of degree $n+1$ equals $x^{n+1}-P$ where $P=Q-x^{n+1}$ has degree $\le n$). Hence
$$\text{RHS} = \inf_{Q\in\mathcal{M}_{n+1}[a,b]}\|Q\|_{\infty,[a,b]}.$$

- For the **left side**: $\prod_{i=0}^{n}(x-x_i)$ with $a\le x_0<\cdots<x_n\le b$ is a monic polynomial of degree $n+1$ whose $n+1$ roots are all real and lie in $[a,b]$. Let
$$\mathcal{S}:=\Bigl\{\prod_{i=0}^{n}(x-x_i)\,:\,a\le x_0<\cdots<x_n\le b\Bigr\}\subset\mathcal{M}_{n+1}[a,b].$$
Then
$$\text{LHS} = \inf_{Q\in\mathcal{S}}\|Q\|_{\infty,[a,b]}.$$

Since $\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{n+1}[a,b]$, taking the infimum over a smaller set can only increase the value, so
$$\text{LHS}\ge\text{RHS}. \tag{1}$$

---

**The minimizer of the RHS.** By the classical Chebyshev minimax theorem, among all monic polynomials of degree $m$ on $[a,b]$, the unique minimizer of the sup norm is the scaled Chebyshev polynomial
$$Q_m^*(x) \;=\; \frac{(b-a)^m}{2^{2m-1}}\,T_m\!\left(\frac{2x-a-b}{b-a}\right),$$
where $T_m$ is the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Its sup norm is $(b-a)^m/2^{2m-1}$.

Existence of a minimizer is guaranteed: $\mathcal{M}_{n+1}[a,b]$ is a closed affine subspace, $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ is continuous, and $\|Q\|_\infty\to\infty$ as the lower coefficients of $Q$ grow, so the infimum is attained. Uniqueness follows from the equioscillation characterization (a best monic approximant of degree $m$ must equioscillate at $m+1$ points, forcing it to be the scaled Chebyshev polynomial).

**Crucially, $Q_m^*$ has all its roots in $[a,b]$.** The Chebyshev polynomial $T_m$ has $m$ distinct real roots
$$\cos\!\left(\frac{(2k-1)\pi}{2m}\right),\quad k=1,\dots,m,$$
all lying in $(-1,1)$. Under the affine map $t\mapsto \frac{(b-a)t+a+b}{2}$ sending $[-1,1]$ to $[a,b]$, these roots map to $m$ distinct points strictly inside $(a,b)$. Therefore $Q_m^*\in\mathcal{S}$.

---

**Conclusion.** Taking $m=n+1$, the minimizer $Q_{n+1}^*$ of the RHS belongs to $\mathcal{S}$, so
$$\text{RHS}=\|Q_{n+1}^*\|_{\infty,[a,b]}\ge\inf_{Q\in\mathcal{S}}\|Q\|_{\infty,[a,b]}=\text{LHS}. \tag{2}$$

Combining (1) and (2):
$$\text{LHS}=\text{RHS}.$$

The equality **holds**. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
